Produced content keeps growing
Licensed content shrank from $12.7bn to $12.1bn while produced content grew from $18.9bn to $20.6bn.
Source: Netflix Form 10-K, FY2023 to FY2025 | Neha M
Content cost grew slower than revenue
+16% vs +34%
Amortisation growth vs revenue growth, 2023 to 2025
Source: Netflix Form 10-K, FY2023 to FY2025 | Neha M
Cash spend ran above amortisation
Cash content spend was 0.93x amortisation in 2023, then 1.11x and 1.08x in 2024 and 2025.
Source: Netflix Form 10-K, FY2023 to FY2025 | Neha M
Free cash flow versus net income
Free cash flow margin was 20.5%, 17.8% and 20.9%. Operating cash flow was 1.35x, 0.85x and 0.92x net income.
Source: Netflix Form 10-K, FY2023 to FY2025 | Neha M

Key findings
1
Revenue grew about 16% a year, from $33.7bn in 2023 to $45.2bn in 2025.
2
Operating margin rose from 20.6% to 29.5% as content amortisation fell from 42.1% to 36.3% of revenue.
3
Cash content spend ran above amortisation in 2024 and 2025 (1.11x and 1.08x), yet free cash flow margin stayed between 18% and 21%.
Source: Netflix Form 10-K, FY2023 to FY2025 | Neha M
Conclusion
Netflix's profit is backed by real cash, with margins rising because content cost is growing slower than revenue.
Watch-point: cash content spend above amortisation kept 2024 free cash flow flat while net income rose.
Source: Netflix Form 10-K, FY2023 to FY2025 | Neha M
